title: Winner of the Linked List Game
statement:
`head` is the first node of a singly linked list with an even number of nodes. Number the nodes from 0: every node at an even position holds an even value, and every node at an odd position holds an odd value.

Group the list into consecutive pairs (nodes 0 and 1, nodes 2 and 3, and so on). Two teams score points:

- Team **Even** gets a point for a pair whose even-position node has the larger value.
- Team **Odd** gets a point for a pair whose odd-position node has the larger value.

Return `"Even"` if team Even ends with more points, `"Odd"` if team Odd ends with more points, and `"Tie"` if their scores are equal.
constraints: The number of nodes is even
Every node at an even position (0, 2, 4, ...) holds an even value
Every node at an odd position (1, 3, 5, ...) holds an odd value
notes:
## Intuition

The game is decided pair by pair, and each pair is just two neighbouring nodes. So one walk down the list, jumping two nodes at a time, sees every pair exactly once. Two counters record the score, and a final comparison names the winner. A brute-force version would copy the values into an array first; the walk does the same work without the copy.

## Approach

1. Start both counters, `even` and `odd`, at 0.
2. Put `node` on `head`. It always sits on the first (even-position) node of a pair, and `node.next` is its partner.
3. Compare `evenValue = node.val` with `oddValue = node.next.val` and give the point to the side with the larger value.
4. Jump `node` forward by two with `node.next.next`; the list length is even, so this lands on the next pair or on `null`.
5. Return `"Even"` or `"Odd"` for the larger counter, or `"Tie"` when they match.

## Example 1, step by step

The list is `2 → 1`. `node` starts on `2`, so `evenValue = 2` and `oddValue = 1`. Since `2 > 1`, `even` becomes 1. Then `node = node.next.next` is `null` and the loop stops with `even = 1`, `odd = 0`, so the answer is `"Even"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is read once.
- Space: O(1): two counters and a pointer.

## Pitfalls

- The pairs are fixed (0–1, 2–3, ...); they do not overlap, so step by two nodes, not one.
- The two values in a pair have different parities, so they can never be equal; one side always scores.
- Return the exact strings `"Even"`, `"Odd"` and `"Tie"`, with capital first letters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `even` | points won by team Even |
| `odd` | points won by team Odd |
| `node` | first node of the current pair |
| `evenValue` | value at the pair's even position |
| `oddValue` | value at the pair's odd position |

narration.2: Team Even starts with no points.
narration.3: Team Odd starts with no points.
narration.4: Visit the pairs: node is the first node of a pair, and it jumps two nodes each round.
narration.5: The first node of the pair sits at an even position.
narration.6: Its partner right after it sits at an odd position.
narration.7: Does the even-position value win this pair?
narration.10: No: the values differ in parity, so the odd-position value is larger and team Odd scores.
narration.13: After all pairs, check whether team Even is ahead.
narration.16: Otherwise check whether team Odd is ahead.
narration.19: The scores are equal, so the game is a tie.
